description: Commercial Bancgroup, Inc. operates as the bank holding company for Commercial Bank that provides a range of banking and financial services to individual and corporate customers in the United States.
description_full: Commercial Bancgroup, Inc. operates as the bank holding company for Commercial Bank that provides a range of banking and financial services to individual and corporate customers in the United States. The company accepts various deposit products, including demand deposit accounts, interest-bearing products, savings accounts, and certificates of deposit products. It also offers real estate, commercial, and consumer loans, such as installment loans, secured and unsecured personal lines of credit, and overdraft protection lines. In addition, the company provides treasury management services, remote deposit capture, internet and commercial banking, automated teller machines, and other banking services. The company was formerly known as Harrogate Corporation and changed its name to Commercial Bancgroup, Inc. in April 1989. Commercial Bancgroup, Inc. was incorporated in 1975 and is based in Harrogate, Tennessee.

financial_summary: Commercial Bancgroup, Inc. is a small-cap financial services business with a $449M market cap on $90M of annual revenue.
Returns on capital run at 12% against a 7% cost of capital, a 5-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $35M in free cash flow — roughly 39 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 1.00× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.4× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 1.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 6.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 54% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sector_headwinds.text: Altman Z in the distress zone (0.4) — the kind of balance-sheet risk that can make a loss permanent
Low reinvestment-driven growth suggests the compounding engine has stalled
Credit cycles and regulatory capital — losses accumulate invisibly in good years and appear all at once, and the time to worry is when underwriting standards are loosest.
Fintech disintermediation — neobanks, embedded finance, and blockchain rails are unbundling the fee streams that traditional banks took for granted.
Interest rate regime shifts — a rapid move in rates can invert the yield curve, crush bond portfolios, and trigger deposit flight simultaneously.
